newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tourism spending rose, market share slipped.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tourism spending rose, market share slipped.

text.p: California's travel and tourism industry expanded in 1996, but the state's share of the U.S. market slipped to a new low, state officials said on Friday.
Visitor spending in California increased 4.8 percent to $57.8 billion last year, and has increased nearly $12.5 billion since 1990, the state Trade and Commerce Agency said.

In 1996, the California tourism industry employed an additional 31,000 workers, an increase of 4.7 percent from the previous year, while tourism payroll increased 3.4 percent, or $400 million, during the same period.
Tax revenues from California's tourism industry also increased, with an overall gain of 4.1 percent, or $100 million, the Trade and Commerce Agency said.
Despite these gains, the state's share of the U.S. travel and tourism market dropped.
An estimated 10.5 percent of U.S. travelers visited California in 1996, according to John Poimiroo, deputy secretary for the Trade and Commerce Agency. In 1989, 12.3 percent traveled to California.
"Aggressive marketing by other states has contributed to this decline in market share," Poimiroo said.
